title: Senior Software-Entwickler (m/w/d) – PHP/Symfony & React – Berlin - Hybrid
description:
Senior Software-Entwickler (m/w/d) – PHP/Symfony & React – Berlin 

Der Plan steht, jetzt fehlst du: Bring unsere Software von Legacy-PHP auf Symfony und React. 

Auf einen Blick 

- Stack: PHP 8.1 (Legacy) → Symfony · jQuery/Vanilla-JS → React · MySQL/MariaDB, SingleStore · Git, CI/CD

- Vertrag: unbefristet, Vollzeit

- Arbeitsmodell: hybrid, 3 Tage Büro / 2 Tage remote

- Standort: Berlin-Zehlendorf, direkt am S-Bahnhof Zehlendorf (S1)

- Produkt: Konsentas, ein Termin- und Vorgangsmanagement für Behörden

- Start: so bald wie möglich oder nach Vereinbarung

Die Rolle 

Unser Kernprodukt Konsentas ist über viele Jahre gewachsen, und das sieht man dem Code an. Das Backend läuft auf PHP 8.1 ohne Framework. Im Frontend stehen jQuery und Vanilla-JS neben React, und automatisierte Tests gibt es bisher wenige.

Wohin es gehen soll, ist klar: Das Backend wird schrittweise auf Symfony umgestellt, das Frontend auf React vereinheitlicht. Bis Ende 2027 soll die Migration abgeschlossen sein. Was dafür fehlt, ist kein Plan, sondern Kapazität.

Du triffst eigenständig technische Entscheidungen, bringst dich in Architektur- und Modernisierungsfragen ein und sorgst dafür, dass die Codequalität mit jedem Release besser wird. Dabei bleibt das Produkt im Einsatz: Wartung, Support und neue Features laufen parallel zur Modernisierung.

Deine Aufgaben 

- Legacy-Module bei laufendem Betrieb schrittweise durch Symfony-Services und React-Oberflächen ersetzen

- Fullstack-Features von der Datenbank bis zum Frontend entwickeln, teils auch als kundenspezifische Erweiterungen

- Bestehenden Legacy-Code pflegen, debuggen und weiterentwickeln

- Code-Reviews durchführen und die Testabdeckung ausbauen

- Mit Entwicklungsleitung und Geschäftsführung abstimmen, welche Bereiche als Nächstes modernisiert werden

- Unsere zwei Auszubildenden im letzten Ausbildungsabschnitt fachlich begleiten (ohne disziplinarische Führung)

- Gelegentlich an Kundenterminen teilnehmen, etwa alle 3–4 Wochen

Nach 6 Monaten … 

… setzt du Features eigenständig um, hast spürbar zur Modernisierung beigetragen, die Codequalität verbessert und bist für unsere Azubis eine feste Ansprechperson.

Dein Profil 

- Erfahrung: etwa 4–5 Jahre in der professionellen Softwareentwicklung (ein Richtwert, keine harte Grenze)

- PHP: fundierte Kenntnisse in modernem PHP 8.x mit objektorientierter Architektur, etwa Dependency Injection, Interfaces und SOLID

- Symfony: nachweisbare Praxiserfahrung mit dem Framework

- Legacy-Code: Du gehst sicher mit gewachsenen Codebasen um. Du refaktorierst, debuggst und entwickelst weiter, ohne alles neu zu schreiben.

- JavaScript/React: solide Erfahrung im Frontend, jQuery schreckt dich nicht ab

- Datenbanken: relationale Datenbanken wie MySQL/MariaDB oder SingleStore und sicherer Umgang mit SQL

- Tooling: Git und Arbeit mit CI/CD

- Sprache: Deutsch auf C1-Niveau, Englisch mindestens B1

- Arbeitsweise: eigenständig, strukturiert, proaktiv und mit hohem Qualitätsanspruch

- Persönlich: Du kommunizierst verlässlich, arbeitest gern im Team, übernimmst Verantwortung, hast keine Angst vor schwierigen Codestellen und gibst dein Wissen gern weiter.

- Abschluss: Ausbildung oder FH-Abschluss zählen bei uns genauso viel wie ein Uni-Studium. Entscheidend ist deine Praxiserfahrung.

Pluspunkte: REST/API-Design und Schnittstellenentwicklung, automatisiertes Testing (PHPUnit, Jest), Docker, Deployment-Pipelines und Cloud, Software-Architektur und Design

-

Patterns, produktiver Einsatz von KI-Tools wie Claude Code oder Codex. Erfahrung mit Software für den öffentlichen Sektor ist nicht nötig.

Dein Team 

Ein kleines Team mit kurzen Wegen: Daniel (Developer Lead), Nico (Geschäftsführer & Projektmanager), der selbst aktiv mitentwickelt, ein externer Entwickler und zwei Auszubildende. Ihr stimmt euch täglich ab. Daniel und Nico übernehmen dein Onboarding persönlich.

Was wir bieten 

- Ein sinnstiftendes Produkt, das täglich in Bürgerämtern genutzt wird, in einem krisensicheren Markt

- Echter Einfluss auf technische Entscheidungen und eine Modernisierung mit klarem Ziel

- 30 Urlaubstage

- Gleitzeit mit Kernzeit ab 10 Uhr, 2 Remote-Tage pro Woche

- Weiterbildung während der Arbeitszeit, z. B. Udemy-Kurse; eigene Vorschläge sind willkommen

- Claude-Lizenz, offen für weitere Tools

- Hardware: Lenovo ThinkPad, offen für Vorschläge

- UrbanSportsClub und JobRad

- Gute Anbindung: S1 und Busse M48, 101, 115

So läuft der Bewerbungsprozess 

- Kennenlerngespräch mit Sara

- Technisches Interview mit Live-Projektarbeit mit Nico und Daniel

- Teamgespräch vor Ort

- Angebot

Über Girona 

Seit über 25 Jahren entwickelt die Girona Softwareentwicklung GmbH in Berlin Software für die öffentliche Verwaltung. Städte wie Berlin, München, Bonn und Dessau setzen seit Jahrzehnten auf unsere Lösungen, Konsentas etwa in Bürgerämtern, Gesundheitsämtern sowie Kfz-Zulassungs- und Führerscheinstellen.

Du willst ein bewährtes Produkt fit für die Zukunft machen? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung.

title: Senior Product Engineer
description:
Your mission

Join our Engineering team and own features from the problem to the shipped product, in a platform used by thousands of construction professionals.

- Own problems end to end: Take a customer or business problem all the way to production. You shape the solution and its acceptance criteria, design the data model and services behind it, and ship it across backend, API, and front end.

- Solve hard backend problems: Our domain is complex — tenders, bills of quantities, and millions of price data points. You design the data models, APIs, and services that handle it reliably and at scale.

- Make product decisions: Decide how a solution should work for the user, down to the interface, which you build on our design system with little guidance.

- Build our biggest bets: Partner with Product and Design on our most strategic initiatives, and own bringing them to life in the product.

- Collaborate across teams: Work with Product, Design, and Data to translate business problems into shipped features.

- Shape our codebase: Architect and implement modular packages and services in our monorepo.

Your profile

- TypeScript, React, Node: Non-negotiable. You have significant professional experience building, shipping, and maintaining complex web applications. You're comfortable shipping across the whole stack.

- End-to-end ownership: You've taken features from a loosely defined problem to real users, deciding scope and acceptance criteria yourself.

- Backend engineering depth: You design data models, APIs, and services, and you care about performance, reliability, and maintainability.

- UX taste: You care how your work feels to the user, and you make sound interface decisions without a detailed spec.

- Product mindset: You're comfortable with ambiguity and focus on what makes the biggest difference for users.

- Sharp problem solver: You look at a complex system, quickly identify what matters, and decide what to do next.

- Bias for action: When you're unsure something will work, your instinct is to find out with data rather than keep wondering.

- Excellent communication skills in English.

Bonus points for

- Experience shipping AI-powered features (LLMs, agents) into a product.

- Experience with our infrastructure stack (AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform) and with CI/CD pipelines.

How We Build: Our Engineering Culture

We believe in a calm, collaborative, and productive engineering environment. We trust our engineers and give them the autonomy to do their best work. Our approach includes:

- Agile & Fast-Paced: We practice trunk-based development with daily releases to get value into our users' hands quickly.

- Quality by Default: We maintain a comprehensive Cypress E2E test suite and enforce strict typing, linting, and formatting rules to keep our codebase clean and maintainable.

- DevOps Mindset: Our well-oiled CI/CD pipeline deploys to AWS via Kubernetes, with our entire infrastructure managed as code using Terraform.

- Collaboration & Transparency: We value open discussion, constructive code reviews, and a culture where the best idea wins, regardless of who it comes from.

Why us?

- Competitive Compensation: A competitive salary above the market average.

- Work-Life Balance: Choose to work 100% remotely or from our modern office in Berlin. We offer flexible working hours to fit your life.

- Top-Notch Equipment: A new MacBook Pro to ensure you have the best tools for the job.

- A Great Team: Regular company off-sites and team events that connect us as people, not just colleagues.

- Job Security: A permanent contract in a stable, well-funded company.

title: (Senior) Finance Manager (all genders)
description:
At Klim, we work with farmers and food companies to make regenerative agriculture scalable and financially rewarding for farmers. Through our platform, we help farmers restore soil health, increase biodiversity and capture carbon while creating new, reliable income streams.

We’re a Berlin-based AgriTech startup backed by $22M in Series A funding, partnering with global food leaders such as Nestlé and Kaufland to reduce emissions across their supply chains and build long-term resilience. Since 2020, we’ve supported 3,500 farmers managing over 900,000 hectares.

If you’re passionate about building a sustainable food system and driving real climate impact, join us and help create a healthier planet!

Your mission: 

As our (Senior) Finance Manager, you will run all aspects of Finance at Klim. From HGB accounting and the monthly and annual close, through day-to-day financial operations, to audits, controlling and finance projects — you own the full breadth of the finance function end-to-end. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with unusually broad responsibility: you are the person who keeps our financial engine room running accurately, reliably and on time, and who continuously makes it simpler, faster and more automated. You are supported by a working student whose work you steer, and you report directly to our COO.

This role is a great fit for you if you are a finance all-rounder who wants genuine ownership of the entire finance function and the opportunity to make a real impact from day one. With a broad mix of strategic, tactical and operational responsibility, you’ll have plenty of room to shape how we work, improve what’s already there and build an automated Finance function.

Your responsibilities: 

- Own our HGB-compliant accounting: run the month-end and year-end close and deliver accurate, timely financial statements with our external accountants.

- Run financial operations end-to-end: accounts receivable and payable, tax-compliant invoicing, payment runs, expense flows and cash management.

- Manage statutory reporting and tax topics (e.g. Jahresabschluss / annual financial statements, VAT) together with our external tax advisors.

- Prepare and manage the annual audit: audit files, documentation and communication with auditors.

- Support controlling and strategic finance topics: management reporting, analyses and spreadsheet-based models that inform business decisions.

- Be the driving force behind the introduction of innovative AI-based processes, building a state-of-the-art efficient and effective finance setup.

- Manage and develop our finance working student.

Your profile: 

- 3–5 years of experience in accounting and/or finance roles.

title: Co-Founder | Growth, Community & Partnerships (m/w/d)
description:
Co-Founder | Growth, Community & Partnerships (m/w/d)

Standort: München (überwiegend vor Ort)
Start: Voraussichtlich Februar/März 2027
Compensation: EXIST Gründungsstipendium, 2.500 € monatlich für Hochschulabsolventen, plus geplante Beteiligung am Unternehmen

Über uns

Wir sind Pierre-Louis Suckrow und Kerim Anater. Unsere akademischen und beruflichen Hintergründe liegen in Informatik, Design & Computation und Human Computer Interaction. Gemeinsam entwickeln wir eine neue Plattform für die Organisation und Zusammenarbeit in der digitalen Musikproduktion.

Unser Produkt soll es ermöglichen, verschiedene Projektstände und ihre Entstehung nachzuvollziehen, frühere Versionen wiederherzustellen und Projekte zwischen unterschiedlichen Produktionsumgebungen auszutauschen. Damit möchten wir mehr Raum für musikalisches Experimentieren schaffen, den organisatorischen Aufwand in kreativen Arbeitsprozessen reduzieren und die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Musikschaffenden erleichtern.

Ein erster funktionsfähiger Prototyp für Ableton Live existiert bereits. Wir sind Teil des WaveLab Inkubators Batch #7 und im Wintersemester Teil der Munich Music Labs. Aktuell bereiten wir unsere Bewerbung für das EXIST Gründungsstipendium vor.

Zur Ergänzung unserer technischen und produktorientierten Kompetenzen suchen wir ein drittes Gründungsmitglied, das insbesondere die Kommunikation nach außen, den Aufbau von Kontakten und die Entwicklung von Kundenbeziehungen mitgestaltet.

Deine Rolle

In der kommenden Projektphase stehen die Weiterentwicklung des Produkts, die Validierung mit potenziellen Nutzern und der Aufbau erster Kundenbeziehungen und Partnerschaften im Vordergrund.

Wir suchen eine Person, die diese Prozesse begleitet und insbesondere den Austausch mit Menschen außerhalb unseres Teams übernimmt.

Mögliche Schwerpunkte sind:

- Communications & PR: Entwicklung unserer Außenkommunikation, Vermittlung unserer Produktidee und Aufbau von Sichtbarkeit innerhalb der Musikbranche und darüber hinaus.

- Community Building: Aufbau und Betreuung einer Community aus Musikproduzenten, Musikschaffenden und weiteren potenziellen Nutzern.

- Partnerships & Networking: Kontaktaufnahme und Beziehungspflege mit Studios, Unternehmen, Branchenakteuren und potenziellen Kooperationspartnern.

- Customer Discovery & Success: Durchführung von Gesprächen mit potenziellen Nutzern, Begleitung erster Beta User und Pilotprojekte sowie systematische Erfassung von Feedback.

- Growth & Business Development: Mitentwicklung unserer Go to Market Strategie, Erschließung erster Kundengruppen und Validierung unseres Geschäftsmodells.

Die genaue Aufgabenverteilung möchten wir gemeinsam und abhängig von deinen bisherigen Erfahrungen und Interessen entwickeln.

Als drittes Gründungsmitglied bist du darüber hinaus an der strategischen und unternehmerischen Entwicklung des Vorhabens beteiligt.

Wen wir suchen

Wir suchen eine kommunikative und eigenständig arbeitende Person, die gerne mit Menschen in Kontakt tritt und Interesse daran hat, ein technologisches Produkt von der frühen Entwicklung bis zum Markteintritt zu begleiten.

Idealerweise bringst du Folgendes mit:

- Erfahrung in einem kommunikationsorientierten Bereich, beispielsweise PR, Marketing, Community Management, Customer Success, Sales, Account Management oder Business Development.

- Die Fähigkeit, komplexe Ideen verständlich zu kommunizieren und unterschiedliche Zielgruppen anzusprechen.

- Freude am Aufbau und an der Pflege von Kontakten und langfristigen Beziehungen.

- Eigeninitiative, organisatorische Fähigkeiten und die Bereitschaft, Verantwortung zu übernehmen.

- Interesse an digitalen Produkten, Technologie und kreativen Arbeitsprozessen.

- Interesse an der gemeinsamen Gründung und langfristigen Entwicklung eines Unternehmens.

Nice to have, aber keine Voraussetzung: 

- Erfahrung in der Musikindustrie oder Kontakte zu Musikproduzenten, Studios, Labels oder Artists.

- Erfahrung mit Startups, Software Produkten oder dem Aufbau von Communities.

- Eigene Erfahrung oder Interesse im Bereich Musikproduktion.

Ein bestimmter beruflicher Hintergrund ist für uns nicht ausschlaggebend. Entscheidend sind die Bereitschaft, sich in neue Themen einzuarbeiten, eigenständig Verantwortung zu übernehmen und die fachliche sowie persönliche Ergänzung innerhalb unseres Gründungsteams.

EXIST Förderung & Compensation

Wir bereiten aktuell unseren Antrag für das EXIST Gründungsstipendium vor. Das Förderprogramm unterstützt Gründungsteams über einen Zeitraum von zwölf Monaten bei der Entwicklung und Validierung ihres Gründungsvorhabens.

Während der Förderung erhält jedes Teammitglied abhängig von der Qualifikation ein monatliches Stipendium:

- 2.500 € pro Monat mit Hochschulabschluss

- 3.000 € pro Monat mit Promotion

- 2.000 € pro Monat mit anerkanntem Berufsabschluss

- 1.000 € pro Monat als Student oder Studentin

Das Stipendium dient der Sicherung des Lebensunterhalts und ist kein reguläres Angestelltengehalt. Die Förderung steht unter dem Vorbehalt der Bewilligung unseres EXIST Antrags.

Voraussetzungen für die EXIST Förderung: 

- Ein Hochschulabschluss, der in der Regel nicht länger als fünf Jahre zurückliegt, oder eine andere nach EXIST zulässige Qualifikation. Für eine Person im Gründungsteam sind Ausnahmen möglich.

- Ein Wohnsitz in Deutschland beziehungsweise die Möglichkeit, während der Förderung in Deutschland zu leben und sich hier anzumelden.

- Die Bereitschaft, sich während der Förderphase in Vollzeit dem Gründungsvorhaben zu widmen.

Weitere Informationen zum Förderprogramm findest du auf der offiziellen EXIST Website.

Wir suchen ausdrücklich ein langfristiges Gründungsmitglied und keine befristete Anstellung. Wir streben eine weitgehend gleichberechtigte Beteiligung am zukünftigen Unternehmen an. Die konkrete Ausgestaltung möchten wir gemeinsam besprechen.

Zusammenarbeit

Wir sind derzeit in München und Berlin ansässig. Für die Gründungsphase möchten wir das Team in München zusammenbringen, um die Produktentwicklung und den Unternehmensaufbau gemeinsam vor Ort voranzutreiben.

Daher suchen wir jemanden, der bereits in München lebt oder bereit ist, für die gemeinsame Gründungsphase nach München zu ziehen.

Da wir uns noch in einer frühen Entwicklungsphase befinden, sind viele Aspekte der späteren Unternehmensstruktur und Aufgabenverteilung noch offen. Diese möchten wir gemeinsam als Gründungsteam gestalten.

Interesse?

Wenn du dir vorstellen kannst, unser Gründungsteam zu ergänzen, freuen wir uns über eine kurze Vorstellung und Informationen zu deinem bisherigen Hintergrund.

Weitere Informationen zum Produkt, unserer bisherigen Forschung und dem geplanten Gründungsvorhaben teilen wir gerne in einem persönlichen Gespräch.

title: Senior People Operations Manager (f/m/d)

bunch is building the backbone of private markets. Your Role

bunch is around 155 people across Berlin, London, and Amsterdam, and Luxembourg, on the way to roughly 200 in 2027. That means four legal entities, four payroll providers, different sets of people systems to reconcile, different compliance environments.

Right now our People operations run 50% on effort. We want them to run mostly on systems. We also want our people data to be trustworthy enough that headcount, attrition, and hiring numbers are the same in every room they're quoted in.

This person will own the operational and data backbone that the rest of the People function depends on.

- Take full, end-to-end ownership of core People Operations topics — including onboarding, offboarding, contracts, leaves, absence, payroll, immigration cases and documentation — from decision-making through execution.

- Design, build, and roll out automated, AI-supported workflows and integrations across our tools — including Personio (HRIS) and Notion — to eliminate manual work and connect our systems.

- Coordinate monthly payroll across Germany, the UK and the Netherlands and in the near future, Luxembourg, with our external providers. You own data accuracy, deadlines and the provider relationships — the providers own the processing.

- Maintain the compliance calendar and the documentation behind it, working with external counsel where local employment law is involved.

- Manage and support our full workforce across multiple contract types and locations, ensuring correct setup, documentation, and ongoing administration for each.

- Be the first line for employee questions on policy, contracts, leave and benefits — and steadily reduce that volume by making the answers self-serve in our handbook.

- Own the documentation and record-keeping behind employee relations cases: case files, timelines, correspondence.

- Proactively identify gaps and inefficiencies in our People Operations processes, and independently drive improvement projects from idea through implementation.

- Maintain accurate, up-to-date HRIS data as a reliable single source of truth, and support strategic reporting and people analytics to inform business decisions.

About You

- 5+ years of experience in People Operations or HR administration , ideally in a fast-paced, international or scaling startup environment

- Proven end-to-end ownership of operational topics across the employee journey

- A strong track record in automation , including designing and implementing workflow integrations or AI-supported solutions in an HR or operations context

- Strong data literacy : you can build reliable reports, spot inconsistencies and investigate until the numbers are trustworthy

- Experience supporting a varied, international workforce across different contract types, legal entities, locations and working models

- Knowledge of German employment law and compliance requirements ; UK or Luxembourgish employment law is a plus

- Payroll coordination experience with external providers in at least one European country, owning accurate inputs, deadlines and provider relationships

- Hands-on ownership of an HRIS — Personio ideally, or a comparable system you have configured and maintained — plus confidence connecting tools such as Notion to build efficient workflows

- Excellent judgment and communication skills , with the ability to act as a trusted advisor to employees, managers and senior stakeholders

- Fluency in English; German is a plus.

Your mindset

- Own it: You take responsibility for outcomes, manage competing priorities and keep your work, decisions and commitments clearly documented and on track

- Aim for impact: You look beyond the immediate request, prioritise what moves the needle and remove recurring work through better processes, automation and self-service

- Empower others: You are professional yet personable, a trusted, approachable partner who communicates clearly, protects confidentiality and holds boundaries with care

- Always be curious: You question inefficient ways of working, think through edge cases and keep learning across systems, data and changing compliance requirements

- Enjoy the ride: You bring warmth, resilience and positive energy, helping people feel supported even when the topic is stressful or sensitive

- Detail-obsessed, in a good way: You get genuine satisfaction from accurate records, correctly filed documents and carefully tracked deadlines, because you know that is where compliance and trust are won or lost.

We're looking for a Staff Data Scientist, Pricing to build the analytical and machine learning capability that pricing runs on, from demand modelling through to the systems that recommend price.

You won't be starting from zero. We've invested in the foundational data and infrastructure that pricing decisions depend on. What's missing is the capability on top: models the business trusts, experiments that settle pricing questions with evidence, and economics defined once so they hold consistently across Commercial, Product and the customer experience.

The arc of the role runs from measurement to prediction to prescription - understanding how demand responds to price, forecasting how it will respond, and ultimately building the models that recommend the price itself.

What You'll Do: 

- 
Build and own the demand and elasticity modelling capability, quantifying how price affects volume across destination, duration, data tier, and customer segment.

- 
Develop machine learning models for demand forecasting and willingness-to-pay, and take them from exploration through to production with the monitoring and retraining that keeps them honest.

- 
Move us from predictive to prescriptive by building the optimisation layer that turns forecasts and elasticities into recommended prices under margin, competitive and partner constraints.

- 
Design and analyse pricing experiments with statistical rigour, and apply causal methods where clean randomisation isn't possible.

- 
Define pricing within our data ecosystem, owning the governed definitions of price, cost and package economics that reporting, analysis and product surfaces all read from.

- 
Partner with Commercial and Finance to connect pricing decisions to margin and revenue, and to size opportunities before we commit.

- 
Set the analytical standard for pricing at Airalo, from what counts as evidence through to how a model or recommendation gets validated before it influences live pricing.

What You'll Bring: 

- 
7+ years in data science, quantitative economics, or applied research, including pricing, monetisation, or marketplace economics work that demonstrably changed decisions.

- 
Experience with dynamic or algorithmic pricing systems in production.

- 
An advanced degree in Econometrics, Statistics, Operations Research or similar, or equivalent applied depth in demand estimation and the identification problems that make naive price-quantity regressions wrong.

- 
Hands-on machine learning experience across the full lifecycle, from feature engineering and model selection through to deployment

- 
Familiarity with optimisation and decision-science methods that turn predictions into recommended actions, whether through constrained optimisation, bandits, or reinforcement learning approaches.

- 
Proven experimentation expertise, having designed and defended experiments with a clear view on decision frameworks and common failure modes.

- 
Experience building analytical capability where none existed before, turning raw data and a business question into something a commercial team uses repeatedly.

- 
Strong data modelling instincts, thinking in reusable definitions and single sources of truth rather than standalone analyses.

- 
The ability to move comfortably between financial, product and operational data and connect the analysis to a financial outcome.

- 
Genuine partnership instincts, translating between analytical rigour and commercial reality so that Commercial and Product come to you early rather than after the decision.

- 
Fluency in the Python ML stack alongside strong SQL, with the engineering hygiene to hand over code that others can run and maintain.

- 
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to make a methodological argument to people who won't check your standard errors.

- 
A self-starter mindset that thrives in ambiguity and brings structure without waiting for permission.

- 
Comfort using AI tools to augment analytical work, with a point of view on where they help and where they don't

Nice to have: 

- 
Experience in marketplace, telecom, travel, or subscription/usage-based businesses.

- 
Bayesian or hierarchical modelling for sparse segments and long-tail SKUs.

- 
Competitive price response modelling, or working with scraped competitor pricing data.

- 
Familiarity with dbt, LightDash, or similar semantic/BI layers.

- 
Experience designing semantic or metric layers consumed by both analytics and production systems.

- 
Experience working in cross-functional teams spanning commercial, finance and product disciplines.

title: Chief of Staff
description:
About Nous 

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

Why we're hiring 

Nous runs on small teams with real ownership and barely any middle management. That's a big part of how about 30 of us became one of the UK's fastest-growing startups. It also means the work of joining everything up has been spread across the founders and leads, squeezed in around their day jobs. Plans, OKRs, closing the hires that matter, the big company pushes: everyone does a bit of it and nobody owns it.

Last week showed what happens when someone does. We ran "crunch week": five days where most of the company dropped its normal work to relaunch Nous as a household agent. Twelve workstreams, one owner each, a short daily sync and a pre-mortem. In a week we rebuilt onboarding and the website, shipped new agent capabilities, and got legal, security and comms ready for launch. As one of the team said afterwards, when we cluster around a problem for a bit, we do loads of work.

We want that pace more of the time, without a founder having to drop everything to run it. So we're hiring a Chief of Staff.

About the role 

You'll work directly with Greg (our CEO) and the founding team, and own how Nous runs day to day: the pace, planning and OKRs, and the big company pushes, plus overseeing hiring and helping land the hires that matter most. You'll sit in the management meeting and get the full picture, including the things that aren't public yet. And you'll have the authority to change how we work: cancel or reshape meetings, and move people and cut scope during a big push.

You enjoy coordinating, but only because it gets things done faster. You'd rather get a decision made today than design a process for making decisions.

What you'll actually do 

- Set the pace. Spot what's stuck, work out why, and get it moving. Usually it's a decision nobody has made yet, so you get it made, or make it yourself.

- Own planning and OKRs. Quarterly OKRs, the weekly management meeting, planning and offsites. Squads run pretty autonomously; you make sure they're working to the same priorities. Each of these should take up less of everyone's time with you running it, not more.

- Own the scorecard. Keep the numbers behind our OKRs current, and say each week what's off track and why. You pull the data yourself (SQL, our BI tool, a spreadsheet) rather than chasing people for updates.

- Run the big pushes. The next crunch week is yours: scope it with the leadership team, pick the owners, run it, and write up what we'd do differently next time.

- Oversee hiring, and help close the hires that matter. Hiring managers run their own processes, and you won't be running ten of them. But you'll keep an eye on all of them, know where every search stands, and jump in where needed. Mostly that's closing the people we really want: working out what they care about and how to win them. Sometimes it's getting a recruiter excited about working with Nous, or unsticking a process that's gone quiet.

- Represent Nous. You'll talk to recruiters and senior candidates from day one. Over time, and where it helps, you'll represent us to partners, suppliers and investors too.

- Automate the boring bits. You'd rather build the Monday status digest with Claude than write it by hand every week. Anything you find yourself doing every week is a candidate for automating.

What this role isn't 

- An assistant. Diaries and inboxes are someone else's job.

- A process role. If your first instinct is a new meeting, template or tracker, this probably won't suit you. With you here we should have fewer recurring meetings, not more.

- A product role. Squads own what gets built, and strategy stays with the founders. You'll be in the room for both, and you make sure nobody's blocked.

- A recruiter. You oversee hiring and step in where it matters; hiring managers still run their own processes.

- A dumping ground for jobs nobody else wants. You'll pick up odd jobs, as everyone here does, but the bulk of the role is above.

What success looks like 

In your first 90 days:

- The company runs noticeably better: decisions get made faster and fewer things stall. Ask the leads and they'd say so.

- Something that had been stuck for weeks has shipped because you got involved.

- You've helped close at least one hire we really wanted.

- Next quarter's OKRs are set, and the scorecard is current every week.

- At least one piece of weekly coordination (the OKR update, the status round-up) runs as an AI workflow you built, and nobody does it by hand any more.

- We have fewer recurring meetings than when you joined.

After a year:

- You've led two or three company-wide pushes that shipped what they set out to.

- The senior hires you helped close have said yes and are doing well.

- Planning, OKRs and the weekly meetings run fine for a month without you.

- Most of the routine coordination runs on workflows and tools you built, not on meetings.

About you 

You've got 4–7 years behind you (perhaps a little more if you've switched careers), probably a mix of a fast-growing startup and somewhere that taught you structure: consulting, BizOps or strategy and ops at a scale-up, a founder's office, or product work where you ran launches across teams. Maybe you've founded something.

You coordinate because you're impatient. You notice the thing that's been stuck for a week, and you're the one who unsticks it.

You're persuasive. You can work out what a candidate is really optimising for and how to close them, get a busy recruiter excited about Nous, and hold your own with senior people outside the company.

You're comfortable with numbers. You can build a quick model, write a bit of SQL or find the right dashboard, and tell a real trend from noise.

AI tooling is already how you work. Claude, Claude Code or similar is where you get things done, not something you tried once.

You write clearly and quickly. Most of this job happens in writing: kick-off notes, weekly updates, closing emails.

You tell people the truth, founders included, and you keep confidences. You'll see salaries, plans and people issues before anyone else does.

You listen and you care, but you don't do politics. This role has more connective tissue with others than anyone else in the business, so by playing it straight and being an honest broker, you are also establishing an important norm.

Low ego. Some of the job is unglamorous and you do it anyway.

Bonus points:

- You've closed hard candidates, or worked in recruiting, talent or BD.

- You've run a company planning cycle, an offsite or a launch end to end.

- You've worked somewhere regulated (energy, fintech, insurance).

- You've automated a chunk of your own job and have something to show for it.

- You are commercially astute or professionally experienced in a deep domain like law or accounting.

How you will grow 

This might not be a forever role, and that's fine. You'll see more of how a fast-growing company works than almost anyone else here, which tends to open doors: running a new category as we expand, leading a function, or a commercial or operations role. Or the role grows with the company. Either way, we'll talk about it properly once you've been here a year.

Remuneration and benefits 

Compelling packages, including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

An environment where you can do your best work:

- 🏢 A great office set up for lots of collaborative working. We already need more whiteboards

- 💻 The equipment / setup / training you need to do your best work (and of course, AI subscriptions, including Claude Code Max tier)

- 🤝 A high-context environment with lots of exposure to the big decisions - be in the room when it happens (literally)

- 🏡 Flexibility around remote work. If you sometimes just need to get your head down, that's fine

- ☕ Very good coffee

- 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house

- 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots!

- ✈ 33 days paid holidays (including bank holidays)

- 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme

- 🚴 Travel benefits, including the cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans

Nous has an office-first culture. That means we encourage in-person working, and most people do work from the office in Farringdon most of the time. We do a lot of brainstorming, problem-solving and interaction within the team and presence makes this more effective. It also helps ensure people have good peripheral awareness and high context. But we are pragmatic not doctrinal about this, and recognise that, sometimes, certain types of work can be better done remotely. Most team members spend 3-4 days a week in the office on average. This role may naturally involve even more presence than that.

The environment 

Most importantly, this is a high-performance, high-agency and high-trust technical environment. Nous is intentionally lean and AI-native, not just in its product but as a company. Everyone is expected to use AI to its full potential, whether that's debugging a system, streamlining a workflow or improving how customers are served. Rather than building layers of middle management, we hire smart, high-agency people and give them real ownership.

We're dedicated to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace, and we actively welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds. Every candidate is thoughtfully considered, without regard to race, religion, gender expression, disability or sexual orientation.

If you don't tick every box but think you'd be great at this, get in touch anyway.

title: Product Manager
description:
About Nous 

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

How we build (worth reading before the role) 

How products get built is changing fast. With AI tooling, a PM can prototype, dig into production data and commit production code to get a change live all in an afternoon. An engineer can own a product area end to end and decide what to build next.

We're leaning into that. Our PMs lean into code and our engineers run products: one of our engineers owns the car insurance targets. We care about whatever gets the job done most effectively, regardless of once upon a time whose job it was meant to be.

We're moving fast and adapting as we go, and we don't have all the answers yet. What should a squad look like when everyone can build? Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out.

About the role 

So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you’d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role.

You’ll take a squad responsible for a key section of our product and service lines and grow them: expand what they cover, understand the levers that drive their performance (automation, new suppliers, what we recommend to members) and increase their commercial value.

Being a Product Manager at Nous is one of the hardest roles we have. The product is complex and we move fast, so you need to be able to hold a lot of context. You'll switch between very different things all day: thinking about OKRs and the plan for the next couple of weeks one moment, getting a PR into production the next, while helping unblock an engineer.

That's also what makes it exciting.

You bring order to fast-moving work, get some sequencing in place so people aren’t each figuring it out on their own, evaluate what’s being shipped, own the reporting and keep the squad’s energy up. You won’t hesitate to make changes yourself, but you won’t be just another builder in the squad either: when you’re heads-down building, you can’t unblock anyone or bring the team together.

Growing a service line here means working across the boundary between product and commercial, so we’re particularly interested in PMs who’ve had real exposure to the commercial side of a business.

Our agent acts in the real world a lot, so saving someone money takes more than great product execution. We also need access to the best tariffs and suppliers, and we have to understand the regulation we operate in. And because Nous is an agent, your nice neat Amplitude funnels don't work: every user's journey can be totally different. So we're after PMs who are excited by everything it takes to make an agentic product work for real households, including the bits that wouldn't traditionally count as "product".

Worth being upfront: we can't tell you yet which service lines you'd own. It depends on the Venn diagram of your particular skill set and the problems we need to solve at the point you join.

What matters most 

We need all of these at once:

- Sharp. You pick things up quickly and enjoy hard problems. Given a messy one, you can lay out what you know and what you'd check first, then change your mind as new data turns up.

- Adaptable. We’re working a lot of this out as we go, so the role and the squad will change, probably more than once. You enjoy that. You pick up whatever’s needed, PM work or not, and you work in the open: sharing rough thinking early and changing course when someone has a better idea.

- Delivery. You bring order to a fast-moving squad: clear priorities, sensible sequencing, people unblocked quickly, and an honest look at whether what shipped actually worked.

- Product craft. You find the real problem behind a request and make the trade-offs explicit. You care about the details of what our users actually see.

- Commercial and analytical. You know what your area made last month, what moved it and what you'd do next, and you answer most of your own questions with data. You think in conversion, margin and lifetime value as readily as in features.

- Energy. You've probably worked at a startup. You move fast, you're happy doing the unglamorous work yourself, and you'd rather ship this week's version than polish next quarter's.

And everyone builds here, PMs included. You'll use AI tooling (Claude Code or whatever gets it done) to prototype, dig into data and ship changes yourself. You don't need to be an engineer, but you shouldn't be scared of code.

What you'll actually do 

- Grow your service lines. Understand what really drives their performance, be able to measure it, and lead the squad to deliver it.

- Set the squad's OKRs and roadmap, get the sequencing in place, and drive fast, efficient execution.

- Evaluate what’s being shipped, and own the reporting: make sure the reports and the data behind them make sense.

- Work across product and commercial: the suppliers and tariffs we can offer, the regulation we work within, and what that means for what gets built.

- Run experiments, and unblock yourself on the analysis without always needing an analyst.

- Get close to members and ops. Read the conversations, sit with the people handling the edge cases, and fix the parts of the journey where people drop out or get stuck.

About you 

You'll likely thrive here if:

- You've been a PM for a few years, ideally at a startup, and you've owned something with a number attached: revenue, conversion, retention.

- You've worked on the commercial side as well as the product side: a P&L, a supplier or partner relationship, pricing, or a whole service line.

- You're comfortable enough with data and code to unblock yourself.

Nice-to-haves:

- You were a software engineer before you moved into product.

- You've worked on a transactional or regulated product: insurance, fintech, energy, marketplaces.

- You've built and shipped your own thing: a startup, a side project, an internal tool that took off.

This probably isn't for you if your PM experience is mostly roadmaps and stakeholder management at a big company, with no number you owned.

How we work 

We keep the middle thin, on purpose. There's barely any middle management, which means fewer bottlenecks and room for exceptional people to have real impact without first being promoted into managing others. It's a real bet, not a free lunch. Instead of a manager buffer, you get lots of context and colleagues who help because they're invested, not because an org chart says so. If you need a clear remit handed down before you can move, this probably won't suit you.

Your first 90 days are built around getting you to real ownership safely: pairing when you want it, lots of context, and people who want you to ship. We celebrate the person who built the unglamorous version this week, not whoever thought of it first.

We're office-first, near Farringdon. We do a lot of our best thinking together and being in the same room helps, though we're pragmatic about heads-down work when you need it.

Remuneration and benefits 

Compelling package including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough to pay real salaries, and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

title: GTM Associate
description:
GTM Associate 

London, 4x days per week in-office

Vega is looking for A-players to help build the commercial engine and take on a revenue-driving seat. You will be a clients’ very first touchpoint with Vega; running outbound, supporting growth and marketing initiatives, and building systems that support hyper-growth.

About Vega 

Vega is transforming the way private markets operate. Alternative asset management is one of the most influential forces in the global economy, with over $20TN in assets today. Over the next five years, the industry is set to grow 3x, but GPs are facing challenges around their ability to handle the investment flows that are coming in. GPs have been completely underserved by innovation, particularly on the investor relations side.

Vega built the industry’s first AI-native operating system, where all client work gets done - from the start of an investor’s journey to its end. We are rethinking how work gets done in private markets from first principles: the opportunity is big, but it’s also niche, high-stakes, and difficult to get right.

Who we are 

We are still at the beginning of our journey. Vega was founded by former investors at Elliott and KKR, and built by talent from the world’s leading technology and financial services firms - including Trade Republic, Revolut, Goldman Sachs, BCG, and more. We have raised $30M so far, with the backing of Apollo, Motive Partners, and 60+ senior executives from the industry. Today, we have over $300B AUM and 30,000 users on the platform, and we have much more left to do.

How we do it 

Vega is a fast-growing startup. We want to make this a career-accelerating place for people with the ambition to build something big. If the below sounds appealing, it could be for you:

- We do not seek consensus. You will be expected to voice opinions and take initiative. Vega's best people do not wait to be told what to do before finding solutions to problems they have spotted.

- We believe bureaucracy is the killer of progress. We are focused on creating the minimum viable process to operate with quality at speed.

- We prioritise talent over tenure. There is no promise of progression without performance – we assess and reward people on impact above all else.

- We iterate fast. We make decisions amid ambiguity and with imperfect information, and we strive to balance committing to a hypothesis with iterating at low ego.

- We play to win. Expectations, intensity and ambition are very high, with every single colleague contributing to Vega's success. This often will not be a 9-5.

We know that this culture won’t be for everyone, and we endeavour to make this clear from the beginning of the recruiting process out of respect for your time. Ask yourself whether the above sounds exciting to you in practice every day, and if it does, we would love to hear from you.

Who succeeds in this role 

We look for people who match our ambition levels, and then raise it further.

In this role, you will:

title: Senior Systems Administrator (Linux)
description:
About Bluestaq Limited
Bluestaq starts with our people. We are looking for teammates who THINK strategically, SERVE the mission and LEAD from wherever they stand. If you bring curiosity, ownership and a thirst for delivery, we would like to hear from you.

Every society runs on invisible systems; Bluestaq is that, for data. Bluestaq Ltd is the UK sovereign subsidiary of Bluestaq LLC (Colorado Springs, USA), and we build the secure data infrastructure that allied operations depend on: mission-critical solutions, flowing through thousands of global users, from ingest to publication in milliseconds, for customers spanning the NATO, Five Eyes and wider allied partners.

We are in our formative years in the UK, building on proven foundations in the USA and Australia. That means real opportunity, early: decisions at your level, and colleagues who know their craft and trust you to know yours.

The Role 
You will own specific Linux systems supporting our NATO delivery on AWS, from configuration and monitoring to upgrades and incident response. You will be the specialist the team escalates to when a fault defeats first-line troubleshooting, and you will improve reliability as well as restore it. 

You will mentor Systems Administrators in troubleshooting and operational hygiene. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports, reporting to the Systems Administration Manager, with a clear technical path to Lead Systems Administrator. 

What You Will Do 

- Own one or more systems or environments, covering configuration, monitoring and alerting, upgrades and incident response. 

- Debug difficult faults, including performance problems, resource exhaustion and integration failures, and take each incident from first symptom to a root cause and a remediation plan that holds. 

- Configure and tune services with secure, hardened defaults, and turn scan output and logs into lasting remediation. 

- Plan and execute upgrades and changes under change control, with realistic risk assessment and a tested rollback. 

- Act as the escalation point for Systems Administrator colleagues, mentor them, and document patterns others can reuse in runbooks and standard operating procedures. 

- Work across engineering, cyber and data teams on cross-functional problems. 

- Take part in UK operational coverage, including on-call rotation and structured handovers with the US team. 

What You Bring 

- Strong hands-on Linux systems administration in complex, secure production environments, with depth in service behaviour, performance tuning and hardened configuration. Experience on Microsoft Azure, VMware vSphere or similar platforms is transferable. 

- Sound networking fundamentals, including DNS, DHCP, VLANs, firewalls and routing, and hands-on identity and access management across directory services and cloud platforms. 

- Working experience with automation and infrastructure-as-code tooling such as Ansible, Terraform, Kubernetes, Docker or Packer, and with patching discipline and configuration compliance in an accredited environment. 

- Curiosity and incident discipline: you diagnose faults under pressure, find the root cause, and record what you found as well as what you fixed. 

- Experience owning systems, escalating only genuinely novel problems, and mentoring less experienced colleagues deliberately. 

- Clear written and verbal communication, including when the news is bad, and confident use of ITSM workflows and platforms such as Confluence and Jira. 

- Judgement with AI tools: applying them where they help, reviewing what they produce and handling sensitive data responsibly. 

Essential Conditions 

- Right to work in the UK. 

- Ability to meet the security requirements above. 

- Willingness to work 10-hour shifts on a four-on, four-off rota, including weekends and bank holidays. Night shifts may follow as further systems come online and the service moves to 24/7. 

- Willingness and eligibility to travel to Bluestaq headquarters in the United States for onboarding, and occasionally to sites across the UK and Europe thereafter. 

Nice to Have 

- Familiarity with NATO structures, the NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA), the MOD or other allied defence programmes. 

- Linux certification such as RHCSA, RHCE or LPIC. 

- CISSP, CompTIA Security+ or an equivalent security certification. 

- Experience with CI/CD pipelines, DevSecOps or Secure by Design delivery. 

- Experience with database administration or data-platform operations. 

- A background in cloud, cyber security or C4ISR environments. 

Why Join Us 

- Workplace pension through salary exchange. 

- Group income protection and group life assurance from day one. 

- 33 days’ annual leave including bank holidays, applied to your shift pattern. 

- Private medical cover and 24/7 remote GP access for you and your family. 

- Professional subscription support and ongoing development. 

Bluestaq Ltd is an Armed Forces Covenant signatory. Service leavers and reservists who know watch-keeping, escalation and operating under pressure will recognise this work. 

Apply 
If you meet most of the criteria, apply through this listing with your CV. 

Join the Mission
Protect data that matters. Build capability the United Kingdom depends on. Launch into operations, not pitch decks.

Bluestaq Ltd is committed to an inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from all backgrounds, including career returners, service leavers, reservists and people underrepresented in defence technology. We recruit on capability and potential in line with the Equality Act 2010. If you need reasonable adjustments at any stage, tell us when you apply. 

We are proud to support the Armed Forces Covenant. Service leavers and reservists who know watch-keeping, escalation and operating under pressure will find this role speaks their language.

title: Staff Tech Lead, Web & Developer Products
description:
Our everyday digital experiences are in the middle of a realtime revolution: chatting alongside a livestream, getting realtime financial updates, or working with colleagues in a shared online space. Consumers now expect realtime as standard, and Ably powers a large part of it.

We put developers first. Our products help teams build, extend, and deliver realtime digital experiences, delivering over 700 billion messages to more than 2 billion devices every month. Teams at HubSpot, Fin, Dialpad, NASCAR, Sportsbet, and General Motors all build on Ably.

Working at Ably means helping build the infrastructure that will shape the next generation of the internet. More of what people do online is becoming live, shared and interactive, which only makes what we build more relevant and more necessary. AI is the latest place that shows up. There's still so much to build, and we'd like your help with it.

About this role 

As the Staff Tech Lead for the Developer Experience team at Ably, you’ll report directly to our CTO and co-own the DevEx vision and strategy. You’ll lead the engineering team that owns our customer-facing web platform - our dashboard, documentation platform, and control plane - transforming it into a world-class experience for our users.

You are a senior, hands-on engineer who’s passionate about building for developers like yourself; someone who’ll obsess over the developer journey and elevate the user experience of the Ably platform. You’ll blend deep full-stack expertise with a strong product mindset, and lead a team of engineers working on initiatives where the feedback loop is immediate, because you and your team are the target users of the very ecosystem you are building.

Ably is an AI-forward organisation and this is a leadership role for an AI-first engineer. You must have confident, hands-on experience of AI-assisted development and be able to define how a team actually works with these tools day to day, and tell the difference between genuine leverage and noise.

Day to day you will 

- Obsess over developer experience. You’ll have broad responsibility for elevating how developers interact with Ably’s platform and services, partnering with the DevEx PM as a unified leadership team to deliver a developer experience that becomes a reference point for the industry.

- Define and lead on AI-first working practices. You’ll be the catalyst and standard-setter for AI-enabled development across the team. You’ll leverage LLMs and AI tools to accelerate velocity, design workflows, set the guardrails and coach engineers to use them well - without compromising on engineering integrity.

- Lead technical execution and vision. You’ll lead a team of five engineers building customer-facing web applications and own the technical architecture and design decisions for our dashboard, docs platform, marketing website, and billing UI.

- Drive a product-first engineering culture. You’ll foster an environment where engineers are themselves principal stakeholders of product features, and obsess over customer outcomes. You’ll challenge the "feature factory" mentality and build a team that takes true ownership of the product.

- Thrive in a rapid iteration environment. You’ll operate in a high-velocity workspace where PMs, customers, and engineers co-create features. You’ll lead the team in working full-stack to iterate, improve, and ship improvements quickly.

- Guide engineering outcomes and quality. You’ll set and enforce high standards for code review, testing, and production readiness. You will participate in incident response and coordinate with the Infrastructure team on platform dependencies and deployments.

- Mentor and grow the team. You’ll manage performance, career development, and hiring. You will hold the team accountable for delivery commitments while providing the mentorship needed to turn engineers into product-minded leaders.

We'd love to talk if you have 

- Real, demonstrable experience leading AI-first engineering. You champion the use of AI as a productivity multiplier for the team, and have led a team that ships with LLMs and AI tooling embedded in its daily workflow. You see AI as an enabler for higher velocity and output, not a replacement for engineering judgment, and hold strong, evidence-based views on what works and what doesn’t.

- Extensive experience leading technical teams in technical B2B SaaS or API-first products, with a track record of product-minded engineering teams that take initiative and ownership of product outcomes.

- A strong software engineering background with genuine full-stack fluency. You must have enough depth across the web stack to credibly lead and challenge senior web engineers. Hands-on experience with React and TypeScript is valuable, but sound engineering judgement and technical gravitas matter more than specific frameworks.

- You have a natural empathy and strong instincts for what developer customers want because you are the target user. You are genuinely excited about building developer tools and can tap into immediate feedback loops. You understand API design, documentation, and the nuances that differentiate a great developer journey.

- Experience at a startup or growth-stage company or adaptability to thrive in a fast-paced, agile environment with a focus on rapid iteration. To be effective in this role you’ll need excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Bonus points if you have 

- Deep production experience building and shipping customer-facing web applications at scale with React and TypeScript.

- Experience delivering solutions used by software developers (developer tooling or APIs) or similar technical personas.

- An understanding of pub/sub and familiarity with distributed systems and event based architectures.

What’s it like to work at Ably? 

You'll join a team of around 60 people, working directly alongside senior engineering and leadership. No layers, no bureaucracy, and real ownership from day one.

Remote-first

We hire the best people wherever they are across the UK and Europe, trust them to own their work, and share decisions and feedback openly. Twice a year, in February and August, we all meet in person, and we expect everyone to be there.

Remote-first comes with trade-offs. On one side: flexibility, no commute, long stretches of focus time, and a wider pool of people to hire from. On the other: it can feel isolating, relationships take effort to build, and you miss the chance conversations an office creates. As our only recruiter, you'll need to manage your own time and stay close to the hiring managers and candidates you work with.

If you do your best work with trust and autonomy, this will suit you. If you'd rather have an office around you every day, it probably isn't the right fit.

Our six values shape how we work day to day:

- Open for all. We default to sharing openly: source, decisions, and feedback, with open minds to match.

- Tech needs humanity. We build with empathy, for colleagues and developers alike.

- Even the best do better. We keep raising our own bar, driven by curiosity, not complacency.

- Bias for action. Once we know enough to act, we act, rather than waiting for certainty.

- Dependable by default. We take real ownership of what we ship and what we promise.

- Bold creativity wins. We treat big constraints as a reason to think differently, not less.

You can read more about how we defined these values on our blog , and see the team behind them on our careers page .

Diversity, inclusion, and belonging at Ably

We believe our differences as individuals are what make us great. Our people are at the heart of what we do, and we encourage everyone to be their most authentic self at Ably: we see inclusivity and openness as fundamental to our long-term success. We encourage applications from all backgrounds regardless of age, disability, gender, sexual orientation, parental status, race, religion, educational background, or neurodiversity. Ably has an amazing opportunity ahead of us, and we want anyone to be able to contribute to it.

If you enjoy working as part of a technology company, value open source, and love solving hard problems, we'd love to hear from you, regardless of whether you fit the job description exactly or not. If in doubt, drop us an email ; ; we're happy to give you advice on your application. 

What you'll get

- A remote-first and flexible work environment. Our London office (next to Old Street) is there whenever you want it. Aside from our company get-togethers, you're welcome to work wherever suits you best.

- Equity. We're a growing start-up, and we want everyone to share in the company's success through our EMI share options programme.

- Enhanced holiday allowance: 28 days of paid annual leave (27 regular days, plus a day off to enjoy your birthday).

- Enhanced parental leave, so you can spend time with your new family member: up to 16 weeks fully paid for primary caregivers and 4 weeks for secondary, depending on length of service. 

- A home workstation budget of £500 on joining (and £150 per year after that), so your home office serves you well.

- A personal learning and development budget of £1000 a year, plus 5% L&D time during working hours to build your skills.

- Private healthcare with BUPA.

- A medical cash plan covering a range of medical and dental costs.

- Mental wellbeing coaching and counselling from Self Space.

- A monthly wellbeing budget via Juno.

- Life assurance and income protection.

- Access to Tech and Cycle to Work schemes.

- A weekly snack allowance for our end-of-week "Need to Know" meeting.

- A fully-paid one-month sabbatical after five years with Ably.

CAIS is the pioneer in democratizing access to and education about alternative investments for independent financial advisors, empowering them to engage and transact with leading asset managers on a massive scale through a wide variety of alternative investment products and technology solutions. CAIS provides financial advisors with a broad selection of alternative investment strategies, including hedge funds, private equity, private credit, real estate, digital assets, and structured notes. CAIS also delivers industry-leading technology, operational efficiency, and world-class client service throughout the pre-trade, trade, and post-trade experience. CAIS serves over 2,500 wealth management firms that support more than 65,000 financial advisors who oversee approximately $8.5 trillion in end-client assets. 

About the role 
We’re looking for a Senior Backend Product Engineer to join our Capital Markets technology team in London. This is a hybrid, hands-on role: you’ll design, build and run systems across Pre-Trade, Trade and Post-Trade, covering Structured Investments, Equity IPOs, Hedging & Monetization, ETFs, and more. 

We put a lot of emphasis on the “product” in product engineer. You’ll work alongside product managers and directly with the business to turn open-ended problems into working software, and the results show up in how a fast-growing company performs. AI is a big part of how we work: the team uses it throughout the development lifecycle and has already shipped several agentic features. You’ll help build the next ones. 

We work in small, autonomous teams using the Kanban principles of optimi z ing flow and limiting WI P. The team owns its work together, from shaping the problem through to running it in production . We collaborate closely with colleagues and stakeholders in New York. Engineers own their work from shaping the problem through to running it in production. While we have access to QA expertise , we consider quality to be everyone’s responsibility , so engineers own testing too. We care about strong engineering fundamentals, especially as AI changes how we build. 

You’ll mostly write Kotlin, working with Spring, Postgres, Elasticsearch and Kafka, and deploying to Kubernetes on AWS through GitHub and ArgoCD. 

Why join us 

- Real ownership : you’ll shape problems with the business, not just pick up tickets 

- Visible impact : your work shows up directly in how a fast-growing business performs 

- Interesting domain : complex, real-world problems across the full trade lifecycle 

- Engineering quality: strong fundamentals and high standards 

- Modern codebase: we’ve moved off legacy, and our systems have been built in the last few years 

Skills & Experience 

- Experience working as a software developer with Java or Kotlin server-side applications 

- Track record of turning business problems into working software, with a clear, measurable impact 

- Experience building and running mission-critical services in production, from CI/CD through to monitoring, alerting and incident response 

- Strong testing habits across unit, integration and end-to-end tests, with good judgment about what to test at each level 

- Strong experience with Spring (Boot, Data, Security), relational database design, REST API design, and Kafka or a similar event streaming platform 

- Experience working AI-first: using AI agents to build software, with an understanding of how LLMs work and good judgement about when to trust their output 

- Technical leadership within your team, including mentoring less experienced engineers and setting and sharing engineering standards 

- Clear communication, including explaining technical decisions to non-engineers 

Nice to have 

- Financial services experience, ideally capital markets 

- Elasticsearch, Kubernetes, Postgres, AWS, Terraform 

- TypeScript and React, and/or motivation to try full stack development 

- Experience building AI or agentic applications 

This role is a hybrid role, with at least 2-3 days spent out of our Old Street office - N1 7LB.

The role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to build the event-processing pipelines and services that turn Nebius product usage into revenue.
You will work on systems that process a continuous stream of usage events, where correctness and failure recovery matter as much as throughput. The output is money: a silently dropped or double-counted event is a real financial error.
Usage of every Nebius product arrives as a stream of events. Our pipelines and services ingest, validate, enrich and price it in near real time, and deliver the results to invoicing, reporting and customer-facing account management.

In this role, you will:

- Build stateful streaming pipelines that compute billed consumption in near real time.

- Develop and operate Go services that ingest usage events, move data between our storage systems and deliver consumption data to users through usage APIs and billing data exports.

- Guarantee correctness under failures: idempotency, exactly-once processing and reconciliation.

- Operate transactional storage, persistent queues and change data capture under high throughput.

- Build reusable streaming infrastructure rather than solving each use case independently.

- Improve the reliability, scalability, latency and observability of the billing platform.

- Take end-to-end ownership of your systems: design, implementation, reliability and deployment.

We expect you to have:

- Strong software engineering fundamentals.

- Professional experience building and operating backend, streaming or data-intensive systems.

- The ability to reason about consistency and data correctness under failures.

- Experience with databases, messaging systems or event-processing platforms.

- The ability to investigate unfamiliar systems and solve problems without an obvious predefined solution.

- The ability and willingness to learn the team's technology stack.

It will be an added bonus if you have:

- Experience with a stateful stream-processing framework such as Apache Flink or Kafka Streams.

- Experience designing streaming pipelines.

- Experience operating services in Kubernetes.

title: Senior GTM System Builder
description:
Help make the world more hospitable 

The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.

You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.

If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.

About the role 

Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:

The commercial team at Mews moves deals through a complex, multi-touch GTM motion. The person in this role owns the systems that make that motion faster, smarter, and less dependent on manual effort — from inbound routing and deal enrichment to Gong-driven coaching intelligence and CPQ automation. This is not a support role for the commercial team. It is an ownership role for the infrastructure they run on.

You will join the Growth team to own an assigned domain within the GTM stack end to end: scoping, building, shipping, and running production systems that move ARR. You will work under staff technical direction but make your own architecture and build-vs-buy decisions within your domain. You will manage vendor relationships, define observability standards, and be the person who picks up the phone when something breaks in production.

What you would do 

- Own the full lifecycle of automation and AI-tooling initiatives within your assigned GTM pod: scoping, building, shipping to production, and iterating based on adoption and KPI data — not just ticket completion

- Build and ship AI-powered pipelines that permanently remove manual GTM work: deal enrichment, outbound research and routing, Gong-driven coaching signals, forecasting inputs, CPQ automation, and proposal follow-up

- Design the prompting architecture and agent logic that commercial reps, BDRs, and AEs interact with daily — reliable outputs for non-technical end users, with observability and error handling built in from the start

- Own operational health of your domain's live systems: first responder when things break, with adoption metrics, error rates, and data quality visibility instrumented before deployment

- Manage vendor relationships at pod level (Gong, Clay, LeanData, ZoomInfo, depending on assignment): SLAs, incident escalation, business reviews, and periodic build-vs-buy re-decisions

- Support other engineers through code review, pairing, and coaching on architecture trade-offs — and contribute reusable patterns and integrations that accelerate delivery across pod

AI Fluency Level 4: In this role, AI is not a productivity layer — it is the product. You will architect and ship LLM-powered agents, enrichment pipelines, and AI-assisted automations that the commercial org depends on. You will make engineering decisions about models, infrastructure, and MCP integrations. You will design prompting systems that non-technical users rely on without ever touching a prompt themselves. The test for everything you build is whether a KPI moved — which means your judgment about where AI is trustworthy and where it needs a human in the loop is part of the work, not an afterthought.

For more information on AI fluency at Mews, please refer to AI Fluency at Mews: A Comprehensive Guide for Candidates on Confluence. 

What you would bring 

- 4 to 6 years delivering production software with measurable commercial impact in a product-driven company (high-growth SaaS, startup, or scale-up)

- Demonstrated end-to-end ownership with strong autonomy: you have defined the approach, navigated genuine ambiguity, and owned the outcome — not executed tickets

- Has shipped AI-powered pipelines or agents in a real operational context: enrichment, routing, summarization, or AI-assisted automation — not just prototypes

- Active practitioner of modern AI development tooling (Claude, Lovable, Cursor, or equivalent) and comfortable working with LLM APIs and MCP integrations — AI Fluency Level 4 or the equivalent hands-on engineering experience

- Hands-on experience building against Salesforce or equivalent CRM APIs: workflows, event-driven logic, and data integrations across multiple systems

- Comfortable owning live production systems: incident response, observability, vendor management, and data integrity — draws no hard line between building and running

- Can translate operational pain into technical requirements and explain technical decisions clearly to non-technical stakeholders

Nice to have 

- Experience in or alongside a RevOps or GTM function — understands what commercial reps actually need, not the idealized version

- Hands-on experience with Gong API, Clay, LeanData, or ZoomInfo integrations

- Familiarity with Nue/CPQ, Databricks, HubSpot, Hook, or Ada
